brief: THE BET. No building in this town casts a shadow on the ground. Nine cast shadows exist and every one is an object - trees, benches, the barrow, the shed, the sundial, the boat, the mill wheel, people; the walls have never called the vocabulary that draws them. Give the town's BUILDINGS their cast shadows, so that a clear afternoon puts half the courtyard in shade and a summer noon pulls it in tight under the eaves. The whole apparatus already exists and is tested: `sunVec()` is the one light vector everything casts from, `shadowF()/shSpread()/shOffset()` fade, WIDEN and retract a shadow under cover (and are all exactly 1 below SH_KNEE 0.32, so a fair day is unchanged in that respect), and `dialThrow(h)` at the sundial is the worked solution for 'where does a point h above this foot land, in cells'. `drawCloudShade()` is the pass to copy in SHAPE: one live multiply, drawn AFTER the items and BEFORE `applyLight`, clipped below the horizon, so people and trees standing in shade are shaded too. A 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome; take the swing. Why now: #130 gave every house its own eave and made the skyline ragged, and nothing downstream has ever read that difference at ground level - this is the roofline finally reaching the ground, and it is the largest change to the wide shot available.
successLooksLike: At 1600x950, seed 42, a clear summer afternoon (try day 13 ~16.9 h, cloudCover ~0.39), the west terrace throws a legible wedge across the courtyard paving with a RAGGED far edge that follows the houses' own eaves, not one straight line. At a summer noon the shadows have pulled in under the eaves; at a midwinter noon they are long; under a full lid they are gone. Grade it as a difference image against a same-code control and quote sd/mean on the PATH.court class, which the WATCH note has at 0.143 and which should rise; the courtyard floor should stop being one tone. The census must NOT move - this adds no structure. Filmstrip 0 POP across dawn and dusk, and legible at 390x844.
avoid: Do NOT put it in the ground cache - the sun moves every frame and `drawGround` rebuilds on a dirty flag, so this is a live overlay or it will smear. Do NOT cast per solid CELL: derive casters from wall RUNS (contiguous spans at a shared eave, solved once where the volumes are built, held in WORLD coordinates) and extrude each run's top edge down-sun as one polygon - a few dozen quads, not thousands. Solve BOTH ends of every edge in world space and `project()` each; a world offset added to a projected coordinate is a pixel and the projection is not linear in it (#138's law). Watch for DOUBLE-DARKENING: `nearShadow`, `drawCloudShade` and `applyLight` already multiply this frame, so measure the stacked result at night and under cloud, not just at noon. And do not let it darken the sky strip or the roofs - clip below the horizon as drawCloudShade does. If the perf cost is real, `probes/ground-cost.mjs` and `frame-cost.mjs` are the instruments; `perf.mjs` is vsync-locked and will report nothing.
